2. Records of the case need not be called for. 

 Let a Rule be issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the accused-petitioners should not be enlarged on bail in GR No. 5276 of 2016 arising out of Teknaf Police Station Case No. 35 dated 25-9-2016 under section 19(1), table 9(Kha) of the Madak Drabbya Niantron Ain, 1990, now pending in the Court of Senior Judicial Magistrate; Teknaf, Cox's Bazar and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 5. Mr Abdus Salam, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioners submits that it is apparent from the FIR and seizure list that the alleged incriminating 7773 pieces Yaba tablet were recovered from an box of a over loaded fish food truck coming from Taknaf to Cox's Bazar and the accused petitioners are driver and helper of the said truck and the owner of the fish food namely, Mohammad Ali somehow managed to escape from the truck keeping his goods in presence of the informant party. The learned Advocate further submits that accused petitioners as driver and helper of the truck have been made scapegoat in this case, in fact, nothing was recovered from the exclusive possession and control of the, accused petitioners, who have been languishing in jail hajot since 25-9-2016 on being arrested by the police and police could not gather any material against them although the investigation has been going on for over a period of 8 months and it is not known as to when the investigation will be completed. He further submits that the materials on record are plainly insufficient to think that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accused petitioners (driver and helper) have been guilty or involved with the alleged offence of carrying and possessing Yaba tablets. Finally, the learned Advocate submits that the investigation officer is compulsorily duty bound to complete the investigation process within 15 working days from the date of arrest of the accused failing which the investigation officer is required to inform the failure along with furnishing reasons for such failure as per mandatory provision of section 42 of the Madok Drabbya Niontran Ain, 1990 although, in the instant case the accused-petitioners were arrested on 25-9-2016 but no police report has been submitted within 15 working days, which was expired long before on 9-10-2016, the 10 is still pursuing the investigation beyond 15 days time causing prejudice to the accused-petitioners and under these facts and circumstance of the case the accused-petitioners are entitled to be enlarged on ad-interim bail to secure the ends of justice. 

 6. However, considering the facts and circumstance of the case and the case made out on behalf of the accused petitioners, 1 am inclined to exercise my discretion in granting bail to the accused-petitioners. 

 Md Khasruzzaman J: In agreement with my learned senior brother judge, I am also inclined to issue Rule in the aforesaid case of alleged recovery of 7773 (seven thousand seven hundred and seventy three) pieces of Yaba tablets; however, since I have reservations so far the order of ad-interim bail of the accused petitioners are concerned as such, I am passing my dissenting view over the said matter. 

 11. By means of section 42Kha(1)(Ka) of the Ain of 1990 on completion of investigation the Investigating Officer is to submit police report within 15 (fifteen) working days of the arrest of the accused-person concerned; however, under section 42Kha(1)(Kha) in case of failure to arrest the accused the Investigating Officer is provided with 60 (sixty) working days from the date of receipt of the order to complete investigation and submit report thereof. Said period can further be extended for another (7+1 = 8) (eight) working days in case of failure to complete investigation but nowhere within the four corners of the said provision of law it has created any legal right in favour of the accused to seek bail in case of failure to complete investigation within the said prescribed period. In other words, section 42Kha having not provided any consequence for non-completion of investigation by the Investigating Officer within time, except to face departmental proceeding, its effect is directory, not mandatory. 

 12. Moreover, time restriction as provided in section 42Kha is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case because as per the First Information Report some accused have managed to flee away from the place of occurrence and that the law enforcing agency has failed to secure their arrest till date. In the stated circumstances, since the particulars of the absconded accused-persons including the petitioners are required to be verified as such, more time is required for completion of the investigation. 

 16. However, the fact remains that the case is still under investigation and the custody period of the petitioners is short. Moreover, some of the FIR named accused are absconding. 

 17. Considering the facts of the case and the offence, as alleged against the petitioners and in the premises made above, I am not inclined to grant them ad-interim bail at this stage. 

 (Criminal Miscellaneous Jurisdiction) 

 Criminal Miscellaneous No. 25392 of 2017 

 Md Mozibur Rahman Miah J: This Criminal Miscellaneous case has been referred by the Hon'ble Chief Justice in view of giving dissenting order by Mr Justice Sheikh Abdul Awal and Mr Justice Md Khasruzzaman on the point of granting ad-interim tail to the accused-petitioners named, Mohammad Hossain (Driver) and Md Rafiq (Helper) while issuing rule dated 6-6-2017 acting on an application filed under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 6. The learned judge further found that, since the provision of section 42 of the Act is not mandatory rather directory one as no consequence has been provided in that section clarifying if the investigation is not completed within the time frame what consequence would follow other than initiation of departmental proceeding against the investigation officer so the petitioners cannot claim to be enlarged on bail if the investigation is not completed within the stipulated time. The learned judge next found that, since out of four accused one of the them has still been on run so the very provision of section 42Ka of the Act is not applicable in the instant case. What the learned judge has further found in his order (mode of recovery of incriminating articles) purely touches the merit of the case and hence I refrain from taking note of the same. 

 13. Record depicts, in the instant case the time limit in both the above modes have already been expired. Now question may crop up whether the accused-petitioners can claim to go on bail on being expiry of time limit as enshrined in section 42 of the Act. It solely depends on the circumstances of the case itself. Since it creates reasonable doubt about the very escape of one of the accused from the well-equipped six armed BGB personnel, then the accused-petitioners well have to be detained till his arrest or filing of police report does not sound any cogent ground in refusing bail. 

 18. Granting of bail does not mean acquitting from charge. While granting bail, the court is to see whether the accused would misuse the privilege of bail and there has been any possibility of his abscontion or he could ever influence the process of trial. None of these apprehensions is apparent in this case as one of the accused has still been enjoying the privilege of bail by giving his appearance in the court and all the FIR named witnesses are BGB personnel.
